_about: The demo video. scripts/make_voice.py turns each line into speech; scripts/record_demo.py runs the scenes live in the real Switch room, speaking each line aloud. Names in braces are filled in from what the room says. Point targets are text in the page; 'in' narrows the search to the newest chat post containing that text.
badge: Live: real Switch room and agents. My messages are typed by a script.

lines.intro: Anyone can call their script GPTBot or ClaudeBot. In August, GreyNoise saw scanners on 824 addresses doing exactly that while hunting for credential files. The real test is the address, checked against the IP lists the AI companies publish. Our team runs that check in a Switch room.
lines.switch: This is Switch. The room was made from our template, with two always-on agents: egress-check, which checks addresses and logs, and abuse-writer, which drafts reports. Switch connects the room to our team's Mattermost.
lines.room: Here is the room in Mattermost. Both agents answered the kickoff. A watcher follows our web server's log and posts every AI request here.
lines.scanner_send: Now a scanner on a rented cloud server calls itself ClaudeBot, and asks our site for its dot-env file. I'm sending that request from a real cloud machine.
lines.scanner_result: Seconds later it's in the room. The name says Anthropic, but the address is in neither of Anthropic's lists. The registry names the cloud company that holds it, and its abuse contact. The post hands the case to abuse-writer.
lines.draft: abuse-writer replies in the thread with the report. It goes to that network's abuse desk, with Anthropic's published contact in copy. It quotes the log line exactly, cites both Anthropic lists it checked, and gives the hash of the quoted line.
lines.ask: Anyone in the room can ask a question. Is this address really GPTBot?
lines.ask_result: It is: the address is in OpenAI's GPTBot list, and Microsoft holds it. The command behind every answer is listed under it.
lines.agent_approve: Only a person can approve a report. If an agent posts an approval, say after a prompt injection, the writer refuses. That rule is in the code, not in the prompt.
lines.approve: When I approve it, the writer records who approved.
lines.approve_result: Nothing is sent. No agent has a tool that sends mail. I check the draft in my own mail client, and send it myself.
lines.outro: The lists and registry answers you saw are real, and fetched live. The room runs from the repository with one command. The link is on screen.
